findings.symptom: The assigned HTML tile displays the LaTeX/TikZ source literally in the Diagram convention section instead of drawing the stated one-wire channel schematic.
findings.suggested_repair: Render the TikZ block through a supported diagram path or replace it with supported diagram markup; retain the wire labels X, Δ, and Δ(X).

candidate_missing_diagrams.classification: editorial candidate; not a confirmed defect
candidate_missing_diagrams.rationale: The definition introduces vertex layers, allowed edges, initial and terminal weights, admissible paths, reachability, and a multiplicative score; a small schematic would make those relationships easier to see.
candidate_missing_diagrams.draw_or_check: Show V1,…,VT as ordered columns; draw only edges E_t from V_(t−1) to V_t with weights w_t; mark α on first-layer vertices and β on last-layer vertices; distinguish a zero endpoint weight as disabled; identify one admissible path and its score as α(v1) times the edge-weight product times β(vT). Do not imply missing edges are permitted.

candidate_missing_diagrams.classification: editorial candidate; not a confirmed defect
candidate_missing_diagrams.rationale: The statement maps hidden-path joint mass to trellis path score and explains that maximizing this score yields a posterior MAP path when evidence is positive; a diagram could connect the factors to the path construction.
candidate_missing_diagrams.draw_or_check: Use time layers t=1,…,T with candidate hidden states; label initial node weights π(s)B(s,y1), transition edges A(s,s′)B(s′,y_t), terminal weight 1; show that one path score equals p(z,y) and that common positive p(y) normalization preserves the maximizing path. Indicate zero factors as absent edges/nodes, consistent with the source.
